articles.title: Ebenezer review – Johnny Depp’s Scrooge tries to exorcise ghosts of business past
articles.summary: The latest film version of the Dickens classic A Christmas Carol is decent enough, though its star is rather better as the legendary miser before redemption arrives. Here for lovers of Dickens – and fans of subtext – is an unexpectedly watchable new movie version of A Christmas Carol starring a…
body: In fact, screenwriter Nathaniel Halpern and director Ti West have put together a perfectly serviceable, faithful adaptation – a tradaptation, if you will – of Dickens’s masterpiece about the hideous old miser saved from damnation on Christmas Eve by the appearance of three Christmas ghosts, from yuletides past, present and future. It sticks to the accepted narrative beats and more or less all the familiar episodes, but with a few twists.

There is a witty and ingenious new prologue sequence in which Scrooge’s equally grumpy partner Jacob Marley, played by Ian McKellen, is still alive, going into a full Stadler-and-Waldorf double-act with his old colleague. (Wait – did The Muppet Christmas Carol inspire this?) And West shows us his scary-movie style by having that scene coming to a disturbing close with a kettle’s eerie whistle as it comes to the boil.
points: The latest film version of the Dickens classic A Christmas Carol is decent enough, though its star is rather better as the legendary miser before redemption arrives.

articles.title: ‘Goats are good. They listen’: the herder who defeated Montenegro’s military – and can identify her cows’ herby burps
articles.summary: To Hold a Mountain tells the incredible story of a woman whose way of life was threatened when she heard her pastures were set to become a Nato training zone. The star of To Hold a Mountain is having trouble with her goats, which keep escaping.
body: “You have to take care of them because they are always searching for their paths,” says Gara, whose Montenegrin is translated into English by Biljana Tutorov, the joint writer-director of the stunning film about Gara’s life in the mountains of Sinjajevina. “But the goats are good, especially when they know the shepherdess. I’m a good shepherdess. They listen to me.”

People listen to Gara too, as Tutorov and her partner and co-writer/director Petar Glomazić discovered eight years ago. Their epic commitment to filming this pastoralist community, whose way of life is threatened, has been rewarded: To Hold a Mountain has swept up prizes on the festival circuit after winning the grand jury prize for world cinema documentary at Sundance earlier this year.

The film-makers first met Gara when she spoke at a rally against the government’s plans to turn a swath of the mountains into a Nato military training and weapons testing facility. “Somebody had to say something, and all men were reluctant,” says Glomazić. “And then one woman jumped on the white horse, took the megaphone, and made an incredible speech. And that was Gara.”

articles.title: Oscar Predictions: Film Editing — ‘You Can See Everything’ Looks to Crash a Race of Past Winners and Become the Third Documentary Ever Nominated
articles.summary: Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars, Emmys, Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis.
body: Best Film Editing Predictions Commentary (Updated: Nov. 12, 2026): Oscar-winning editors are occupying these early days of the Oscar race.

Jennifer Lame (“Oppenheimer”) leads with “The Odyssey,” followed by Joe Walker for the still yet-to-be-seen “Dune: Part Three” (he won for “Dune” and was also nominated for “12 Years a Slave” and “Arrival”). On their heels is Mikkel E.G. Nielsen (“Sound of Metal”), who was also nominated for “The Banshees of Inisherin” and is reunited with Martin McDonagh on “Wild Horse Nine.”

Two-time nominee Yorgos Mavropsaridis (“The Favourite,” “Poor Things”) and Anthony Boys, who would be a first-time nominee, round out the early favorites with “The Invite.” After becoming a box-office smash, Adam Locke-Norton is in the conversation with the three-hour nonfiction epic “ You Can See Everything.” He would be the third person to garner a nomination for film editing, after “Woodstock” (1970) earned nominations for editing (and sound), and “Hoop Dreams” (1994).

articles.title: You can see everything on this list: the 20 most jaw-dropping documentaries – ranked!
articles.summary: Ahead of the UK release of Nathan Fielder’s hotly anticipated Elizabeth Holmes film, we count down the most shocking and affecting true stories ever committed to cinema.
body: A 50-second dispatch from daily life blew the whistle on the approaching juggernaut of cinema and its unbeatable horsepower of verisimilitude. But if we must be strictly factual about the iconic Lumière brothers’ short, the anecdote about audience members fleeing their seats in fear of being crushed by the oncoming locomotive probably never happened.

The dramatic re-enactment is the car chase of the documentary industry: a crude way of keeping our attention. But by using rotoscoped animation, Keith Maitland’s riveting account of the 1966 mass shooting at the University of Texas completely revitalises the re-enactment as part of the documentary toolkit. It leaves us prone under the killer’s crosshairs with the emotional immediacy of a thriller and an oddly elegiac comedown.

articles.title: Peacock Sets ‘Love Trapped: The Case of Laura Owens’ Documentary About ‘Bachelor’ Star Clayton Echard Scam
articles.summary: Peacock has announced a new, four-part documentary “Love Trapped: The Case of Laura Owens,” based on the hit 2026 podcast “Love Trapped.” Premiering sometime in 2027, the docuseries tells the story of former “Bachelor” star Clayton Echard, whose one-night stand with a woman named Laura Owens…
body: Per the logline, “‘Love Trapped: The Case of Laura Owens’ follows an astonishing story when Laura meets Clayton through a potential real estate deal and after their short connection, she tells him she’s pregnant with his twins. Their private dispute erupts into a nationally followed story fueled by citizen sleuths and social commentators that join the media firestorm that implodes into a shocking trail of deception, legal threats and public humiliation. The deeper the investigation goes, the more unbelievable the revelations become, while raising a disturbing question: when does the desire to be loved turn into an obsession?”

The Peacock series boasts exclusive interviews that bring together Echard, his legal team, Owens’ mother and other men targeted by Owens. Podcast host Stephani Young and the online detectives who helped unravel the story also appear in the doc. Plus, for the first time, Owens shares her own perspective on what transpired.

“Love Trapped: The Case of Laura Owens” is executive produced by Nancy Glass, Erin Lee Carr and Keayr Braxton for Glass Entertainment Group, as well as Danny Passman for Crybaby Media. Braxton also serves as director.

articles.title: Outlook Outage: Microsoft’s Email Service Goes Down Nationwide
articles.summary: Microsoft’s Outlook email service suffered a massive outage Thursday, affecting users across North America and potentially other regions. “We’re investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas,” the company’s…
body: Microsoft ‘s Outlook email service suffered a massive outage Thursday, affecting users across North America and potentially other regions.

User reports of problems with Microsoft Outlook began spiking at around 12:39 p.m. ET, according to monitoring platform Downdetector. As of 1:09 p.m. ET, more than 129,000 error reports had been logged with Downdetector.

At 1:35 p.m. ET, the Microsoft 365 Status account provided an update: “We’ve determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors.” The account also said the company has “begun redistributing connection traffic across our broader worldwide infrastructure to help balance the load.” Microsoft’s Service Health Status page also said teams are “reviewing an unexpected increase in a specific type of service traffic to determine whether it’s contributing to the elevated load.”
Variety has reached out to Microsoft for more information about the problems.
points: Microsoft’s Outlook email service suffered a massive outage Thursday, affecting users across North America and potentially other regions.

articles.title: Victorian Psycho review – Maika Monroe has a blast in unsteady horror romp
articles.summary: The It Follows and Longlegs star tears into the role of a murderous governess in this hit-and-miss adaptation of Virginia Feito’s gory novel. It’s not that hard to figure out why a lower-class woman toiling away in Victorian England would be so easily driven to violently murder everyone around her.
body: As Winifred Notty (Maika Monroe) fills the frame in Victorian Psycho, heading to a new job as governess for a rich family, it’s easy to be on her side. Even as her murderous impulses start to rear their head, they’re made somewhat understandable, although Winifred isn’t just a woman reacting to the various injustices of the time – she’s one responding to a demon within her, a darkness she has chosen to embrace rather than resist. Darkness is her friend, a protection against harm, and a way to possess some sort of control in a world that has denied her any of it.

The actor has become known as a bit of a scream queen (an all too easily crowned title these days) ever since she broke out in It Follows, but despite roles in hits such as Longlegs and Watcher, she’s never really been afforded that much to do beyond looking petrified. Maybe that’s why it feels like she has so much more to give and prove here, really tearing into a character that requires her to do the petrifying. It’s not just the malevolent soundscape that makes it seem like there is an evil within her but Monroe’s unearthly contortions, an all-in, all-body performance that avoids slipping into histrionic silliness.

articles.title: How much art does your council own and is it locked away or on display?
articles.summary: More than 500,000 pieces of art are owned by 225 councils, the BBC finds, but most of it is storage.
body: Fewer than one in 20 artworks owned by English councils are on public display, the BBC has found.
More than 500,000 pieces of art are held in the collections of 225 councils, but the vast majority is being kept in storage.
Local authorities remain "the biggest single constituent of public funding for arts and culture", according to the chief executive of the charity Art UK.
Yet many face a strain on storage space and resources, with a real-term fall in spending for museums leading to challenges in displaying council-owned art.

articles.title: Duran Duran’s Roger Taylor Retires From Group After Tinnitus Diagnosis: “I Must Now Listen to My Body and My Doctors”
articles.summary: "Playing drums in this band has been the joy of my life, and I’ll never be able to properly thank the fans for the love they’ve shown us over the years," Taylor said.
body: Duran Duran drummer Roger Taylor is retiring from the band, and from drumming, the group announced on Thursday, after Taylor was recently diagnosed with tinnitus.

‘I couldn’t have asked for a better final chapter, with so many special moments that I’ll treasure forever,” he continued. “I move on with enormous pride, and with nothing but love for Simon, Nick and John.”

Taylor first joined Duran Duran during the group’s early days in 1978, appearing on the band’s first three albums before leaving the group in 1985.
